subject: religious-studies
title: Christmas and Easter
welcome_lead: Celebrate the two biggest Christian festivals: Christmas and Easter.
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure on Christmas and Easter, the major Christian festivals.
final_note: You can now describe Christmas and Easter and what they mean to Christians.

concepts.def: Story of Jesus's birth in Bethlehem.
Four weeks before Christmas, preparing for Jesus.

walkthroughs.body_html: Christmas is celebrated on 25 December. It remembers the birth of Jesus in Bethlehem. Christians attend church services, sing carols, and many enact the nativity story with shepherds, angels and wise men. The four weeks before are called Advent.

Easter is the most important Christian festival. It marks Jesus's death on Good Friday and his resurrection on Easter Sunday. It comes after 40 days of Lent — a time of fasting, prayer and giving things up.

Christmas symbols include trees, lights, stars and gifts (remembering the wise men's gifts to Jesus). Easter symbols include eggs (representing new life) and the cross. Both festivals mix Christian meaning with older traditions.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between act and rule utilitarianism?
options: Act utilitarianism judges each individual action by its consequences; rule utilitarianism follows rules that, if generally adopted, would produce the most good — sacrificing case-by-case calculation for predictability and fairness.
Act utilitarianism is about action movies and rule utilitarianism is about laws.
Act and rule utilitarianism are basically the same approach.
Secularisation means the separation of church and state.

mcqs.q: How do samsara, karma and moksha fit together in Hindu thought?
options: Samsara, karma and moksha are three separate Hindu deities.
Act utilitarianism is about action movies and rule utilitarianism is about laws.
Moksha is the Hindu word for heaven.
Samsara is the cycle of rebirth; karma is the law of action and consequence that drives rebirth; moksha is liberation from samsara — these form a connected chain, not three independent ideas.

mcqs.q: What does the secularisation thesis claim?
options: Secularisation means the separation of church and state.
Moksha is the Hindu word for heaven.
That as societies modernise, religion declines in social significance — though sociologists now debate this, since global religion has not declined uniformly.
Secularisation means everyone in modern countries is now atheist.
